ground_truth.label: human-annotated
purpose: calibration and selective prediction per language on the same items
comparison between judges and between languages on parallel rows
caveats: translated parallel data, not native traffic; labels from SLURP annotation carried over by localisation
public since 2022: probably in the pretraining data of the judges audited

SLURP's utterances are requests to a home voice assistant collected for a research corpus, not production traffic; one intent label each, and MASSIVE publishes no inter-annotator agreement on the intent labels

localised from en-US by translators (FitzGerald et al. 2023 describe professional translators; the upstream card names each localiser by an obfuscated MTurk worker ID) and judged by up to three workers of the locale: 120 of 2974 rows have at least one of the localisation judges answering No to 'Does the sentence match the intent?', 19 a majority; _meta.intent_judgments keeps the scores (0 No, 1 Yes, 2 It is a reasonable interpretation of the goal); ca-ES was added in MASSIVE 1.1, after the paper, which does not describe its localisation
options: the 60 MASSIVE intent identifiers in alphabetical order, without definitions; instructions in criteria.language (en) whatever the locale of the text

2933 distinct texts in 2974 rows (case and whitespace ignored); rows 1 and 806 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 12 and 248 hold one text up to case or whitespace, same label; rows 17 and 1426 hold one text up to case or whitespace, labelled calendar_query / datetime_query;
